The Petitioner and the Respondents were directed to file their replies, and certain information/clarification were sought from the Petitioner as well as Respondent No. 2/ GRID Controller of India Limited (POSOCO). Respondent No. 2 filed the reply to the Petition on 6.2.2024. 5. In response to the Commission’s query regarding any other Change in Law and Force Majeure claims under the TSA, the Petitioner submitted that it has not filed any Petition in regard to the force majeure and/or other Change in Law claims. The Petitioner further submitted that the Change in Law events in respect of which the Petitioner is seeking the verification of the calculation of their impact under CIL Rules are post the notification of CIL Rules, which, as such, do not apply to the events which have occurred prior to their notifications. In response to the another query of the Commission regarding dealing with CIL claims (as occurred during construction period) and Force Majeure claims together, the Petitioner submitted that while the Petitioner would file its Petition in regard to its force majeure and/or _residua_ l Change in Law claims, if required, it may not be tagged with the present Petition as it would be adjudicatory proceedings, whereas the scope of the present matter is limited to the verification of the calculation of the impact due to certain Change in Law events under the CIL Rules. The Commission decided to hear the present Petition, along with the Force Majeure petition (which will be filed by the Petitioner soon), together as the Petitioner’s claims relate to the same project. 15. The matter was again heard by the Commission, and the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondents made detailed submissions in the matter. However, the hearing could not be completed due to a paucity of time. The Petitioner was directed to submit certain documents and RoW-related information in the matter. Further, the Respondent LTTCs, i.e. Respondent Nos. 1 to 3, were also directed to file certain information/clarification on affidavits as called for in the RoP dated 29.4.2024. 17. The Petition was mentioned by the learned counsel for the Petitioner for urgent listing. The Commission acceded to such a request and directed the Petitioner and Respondent, GUVNL, to furnish certain additional information on an affidavit. Also, the Commission granted liberty to the Respondent, MPPMCL, to file its reply in the matter. 20. The matter was argued at length by the parties. The Petitioner was directed to clarify/furnish certain documents/information, _inter alia,_ in relation to the power of DC/DM to determine the RoW compensation. In response, the Petitioner filed its affidavit dated 26.12.2024. 21. The matter was argued at length by the parties. During the course of the hearing, the learned Senior counsel for the Petitioner mainly submitted as under: 24. After a comprehensive hearing from both sides, the matter was reserved for order, and the parties were directed to file their respective written submissions. The Commission directed the Petitioner to file certain information on an affidavit. In compliance with the same, the Respondents, GUVNL and MSEDCL, filed their written submissions on 8.3.2025 and 25.2.2025, respectively. Further, the Petitioner filed its written submissions and its compliance affidavit on 8.3.2025. 28. The Petitioner, LVTPL, has filed rejoinders to the reply filed by the Respondents and also submitted the RoP compliances in the matter as directed by the Commission. The brief contentions of the Petitioner are summarised as under: ## **Issue No.1: Whether the Change in Law claims made by the Petitioner are maintainable, given the delay in achieving the COD of the Project? If so, to what extent?** 30. Before we proceed to examine the above issues, it may be noted that another preliminary issue involved in this case, i.e., what is the scope & object of CIL Rules and whether the Commission can adjudge the merits of the Change in Law claims made by the Petitioner, was argued commonly by the parties in this case and in Petition No. 131/MP/2024 (Mumbai Urja Marg Limited v. MSEDCL and Ors.) and by order dated 20.4.2025 in Petition No. 131/MP/2024, the said issue has already been answered in detail. The findings therein squarely apply to this case and are not repeated herein. ## **Issue No.1: Whether the Change in Law claims made by the Petitioner are maintainable, given the delay in achieving the COD of the Project? If so, to what extent?** 34. We have considered the submission made by the parties. As the Petitioner is seeking the relief in respect of the Change in Law events that occurred during the Construction Period, it is pertinent to refer to the relevant provisions of the TSA governing the Change in Law relief during such period as reproduced hereunder: Proceedings dated 3.1.2024 to tag the instant Petition along with another Petition to be filed in future seeking Force Majeure and Change in Law reliefs. Undoubtedly, in terms of the aforesaid order of the APTEL, the Commission is required to decide upon the present Petition independently of the Petition to be filed by the Petitioner in future; however, that does not permit the Petitioner to claim the Change in Law relief beyond the terms of the TSA. APTEL’s aforesaid order cannot be construed to mean that the Commission is required to examine the claims of the Petitioner even if they do not fall within the entitlement criteria prescribed in the TSA. The APTEL, in the said order, has categorically observed that it has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the dispute, or on the scope and purport of the Rules.
